messages.content: Write the welcome page new engineers see on their first day at a software company. Around 250 words.

# Welcome

You're here. Someone has already assigned you a laptop, a badge, and a mentor who blocked out this afternoon for you, so the first thing to do is go find them.

Day one is deliberately light. Get your accounts working, run the setup script in `platform/bootstrap`, and if it fails — it fails for about a third of new hires, usually on the VPN cert — say so in #new-here instead of quietly debugging for four hours. That script's failure rate is our bug, not yours.

Ship something small this week. It doesn't matter what. Fix a typo in the docs, tighten an error message, delete a dead flag. The point is to walk the whole path once: branch, review, CI, deploy, and the dashboard where you watch your change land. Everyone here remembers their first deploy. Nobody remembers what it did.

A few things worth knowing early. We review code hard and people gently. Questions in public channels beat DMs, because the answer outlives the conversation. A meeting with no agenda can be declined, and nobody will hold it against you. When you don't know something, say so in the first ten minutes rather than the first ten days.

You were hired for judgment we haven't seen work yet, so use it early. If something here looks broken or stupid, write it down while it still looks that way to you. That clarity fades in about six weeks, and then you're one of us and can't see it anymore.

The coffee is on the second floor and it's bad. Sorry.

---

258 words. Two details are placeholders you'll want to swap for real ones: the `platform/bootstrap` script path and the `#new-here` channel. The VPN-cert failure rate is invented — either replace it with your actual sore spot or cut the clause, since a made-up number is worse than no number.

Checked against this repo's `slopwatch` ruleset: passes clean.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
# Welcome

Your laptop, badge, and mentor already exist. The mentor cleared their afternoon for you, so start by finding them.

Day one is thin on purpose. Get logged into everything, run `platform/bootstrap`, and when it breaks (it breaks for roughly a third of new hires, usually at the VPN cert) post in #new-here rather than grinding on it alone until dinner. A setup script that fails is our defect, not a test of you.

Try to ship something this week. Anything. A typo in the docs, a clearer error string, a feature flag nobody has read in two years. What matters is walking the full route once: branch, review, CI, deploy, and the dashboard where you watch it land. People remember their first deploy for years. Nobody remembers what was in it.

Some things you'd otherwise learn by bruising. Code gets reviewed hard; people get treated gently. Ask in the open channel instead of a DM, because an answer in public keeps working after the conversation ends. You can decline a meeting that arrives without an agenda, and no one will think less of you. When you're lost, say so in the first ten minutes, not the first ten days.

We hired you for judgment we haven't watched work yet, so start spending it now. If something here looks broken or dumb, write it down while it still looks that way to you. That view goes cloudy in about six weeks. After that you're one of us and you can't see it anymore.

Coffee's on two. It's bad. Sorry.
